properties.digitized_from: Draft EIR Figure 2-2, "Project Site Sub-Areas and Ownership" (Potrero Power Station Mixed-Use Development Project Draft EIR, Case No. 2017-011878ENV, October 2018, p. 2-6), which shows the Port-owned "Port sub-area" (SF Port ownership, ~2.9 acres total in 3 non-contiguous pieces) at true scale with a north arrow and a 400-ft scale bar.
properties.digitization_method: Georeferenced by matching one high-confidence real-world corner (the Illinois St / 22nd St property corner, matched to this project's own fetched data.raw/parcels.geojson block 4175 boundary vertex at lon -122.387166171, lat 37.757917868) plus the figure's printed scale bar, assuming north-up with no rotation. CORRECTED 2026-09-13: the original scale-bar reading (400 ft measured at 516 px = 0.7752 ft/px) placed this polygon's centroid essentially on top of the real Sophie Maxwell Building address on Maryland St -- geographically implausible for a bay-side open space parcel, and flagged as wrong by direct user review. Re-derived the scale independently via OpenStreetMap Overpass API ground truth (real distance 934.7 ft between the 22nd St/Illinois St and 23rd St/Illinois St intersections, measured at 733 px between the same two intersections in the source figure) = 1.2752 ft/px, ~1.64x the original reading. CLIPPED TO REAL SHORELINE 2026-09-13: the rescaled convex-hull trace was a 6.4-acre pointed/diamond shape that visibly didn't follow the real waterfront's curve (flagged by the user) and overshot the EIR's stated ~1.6 acres for this piece by 4x -- a size error the rescale introduced and this project failed to re-check at the time. Clipped the traced polygon against the real Port jurisdiction boundary (data/raw/port_jurisdiction.geojson, via src/block_fit.py's clip_to_jurisdiction()), which traces the actual property/water line -- the same real-boundary-fitting approach block_fit.py already applies to streets, applied here to the shoreline. DE-SPIKED 2026-09-13: the raw clip left a ~90m thin spike where the hand-traced land-side edge grazed a real kink in the jurisdiction boundary at a shallow angle -- confirmed against real satellite imagery (ESRI World Imagery) that no real point of land exists there, just a straight riprap shoreline. Rather than hand-edit that one vertex, generalized clip_to_jurisdiction() itself to apply a morphological opening (erode 10m, dilate 10m back, in EPSG:3857) after the intersection, which erases any sliver narrower than ~20m while leaving the real boundary-following edge untouched -- a fix to the shared tool, not a one-off patch, so any future shoreline clip gets the same spike protection. Final shape simplified (tolerance 0.00003 deg) to 10 vertices, 1.56 acres -- within a few percent of the EIR's ~1.6 acres. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: regulatory_context said BCDC issued the non-material amendment 2019.006.02 on June 19, 2025; the BCDC permit application tracker gives June 19, 2025 as the date the application was received and June 26, 2026 as the date issued, and the property has been corrected. The why_no_real_parcel statement that this land cannot appear in DataSF Parcels is now worded as our inference from the Draft EIR footnote. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, why_no_real_parcel reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE ONLY -- digitized from an illustrative planning figure, not a surveyed record, then clipped to the real Port jurisdiction boundary on its water-facing side and opened to remove a spike artifact (see digitization_method). The corrected centroid falls east of the real Sophie Maxwell and UCSF Block 2 parcels, consistent with a bay-side location, and area now closely matches the EIR's stated ~1.6 acres for this piece. Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly tens of meters on the land-facing sides (still convex-hull-smoothed over the true shape there), but the water-facing edge is now a real boundary, not hand-traced. Do not use for anything requiring exact boundaries.'; why_no_real_parcel: 'This land has no Assessor's Block/Lot number at all -- confirmed directly in the same Draft EIR, footnote 1, p. 2-5: "The Port sub-area, and City sub-area described below, are not assessed properties, and therefore do not have assigned Assessor's Block numbers." It would therefore not be expected to appear in DataSF's Parcels - Active and Retired dataset or to join via status.csv/blklot (our inference from that footnote; a DataSF spatial query over the Port sub-area was not run to confirm).'.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE ONLY -- digitized from an illustrative planning figure, not a surveyed record, then clipped to the real Port jurisdiction boundary on its water-facing side and opened to remove a spike artifact. The corrected centroid falls east of the real Sophie Maxwell and UCSF Block 2 parcels, consistent with a bay-side location, and area now closely matches the EIR's stated ~1.6 acres for this piece. Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly tens of meters on the land-facing sides (still smoothed into a convex outline over the true shape there), but the water-facing edge is now a real boundary, not hand-traced. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
properties.why_no_real_parcel: This land has no Assessor's Block/Lot number at all -- confirmed directly in the same Draft EIR, footnote 1, p. 2-5: "The Port sub-area, and City sub-area described below, are not assessed properties, and therefore do not have assigned Assessor's Block numbers." It would therefore not be expected to appear in DataSF's Parcels - Active and Retired dataset or to be matched to an Assessor block/lot (Pier & Point's inference from that footnote; a DataSF spatial query over the Port sub-area was not run to confirm).
properties.regulatory_context: Prequel Park is the ~2-acre interim open-space project (BCDC Application 2019.006.02, a non-material amendment for which BCDC received the application on June 19, 2025 and issued the amendment on June 26, 2026 per its permit application tracker; SF Port Commission Resolution 25-70, Nov 18, 2025, amending Lease L-16662 with California Barrel Company LLC) of which ~0.4 acres sits on this Port sub-area land near the future recreational dock. Construction targeted Q3 2026, public opening targeted Q3 2027 per the Port's Nov 14 2025 memo (Calendar Item 10A).

properties.digitization_method: NEWLY ADDED 2026-09-16 -- user pointed out that the already-tracked 'Prequel Park (Port sub-area)' polygon (0.4 acres, near the pier's point/breakwater) should connect to Blocks 4 and 9 and to Humboldt Street Plaza, and should not overlap Block 9. That file's own regulatory_context already noted it covers only ~0.4 of a ~2-acre 'Prequel Park' interim open-space project (SF Port Commission Resolution 25-70, Nov 18 2025, amending Lease L-16662) -- the other ~1.6 acres sits on Potrero Power Station's own land (not Port jurisdiction), which had never been separately tracked. A construction-pipeline document (Spring 2026 dev forecast) independently describes this same project as a '2-acre Waterfront Park', strongly suggesting this Power-Station-land portion is the same physical shoreline corridor already traced (less precisely, and for a different purpose) as this dataset's separate 'Waterfront Park' feature (a D4D-diagram-labeled, long-term planning feature, sourced and georeferenced completely differently). Built this connector polygon by combining two already-validated sources rather than re-tracing from scratch: (1) the WEST/inner edge uses Block 4, Humboldt Street Plaza, and Block 9's own already-committed corners directly, so it shares an exact boundary with all three and cannot overlap Block 9 by construction; (2) the EAST/shoreline edge reuses Waterfront Park's own previously satellite-color-validated outer-shoreline trace (see that file's digitization_method for how it was built) between Block 4's latitude and Prequel Park (Port sub-area)'s own northernmost point, where the two pieces meet and touch -- except for a ~20m notch in that trace (its own vertices between the point at lon -122.38137/lat 37.75663 and the point at lon -122.38137/lat 37.75629) that pre-dated Block 9's GDAL/TPS correction and dipped into Block 9's real footprint; dropped those points since the west-edge chain now defines that boundary directly. STATUS CORRECTED 2026-09-24: this record's own dossier (data/records/prequel_park_power_station_subarea.json) had, since its creation, carried a summary and milestone history saying no source confirms construction has started, and its own open_questions explicitly flagged this file's 'under_construction' status as wrong ('Recommend planned until a dated source appears') -- that recommendation was never applied. A site visitor caught the resulting bug directly: the site showed 'under construction' today but reverted to 'planned' a couple of years into the future on the timeline scrubber, because the only real dated milestone with a status is the 2020-04-21 entitlement ('planned'), and the record's own future-projection milestone for 2026 is itself expected+'planned' (construction hasn't started yet, per every source), while the live status field alone (read only exactly at 'today') was stuck on the older, unsourced 'under_construction' value. Corrected to 'planned' to match the record's own sourced research and remove the contradiction; sibling record 'Prequel Park (Port sub-area)' already correctly says 'planned'. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: this file cited no source (source_doc_urls was empty); it now lists the Port Commission memo of Nov 14, 2025 (Calendar Item 10A), the final D4D and the SF Chronicle of May 22, 2025. (1) The Port Commission adopted Resolution 25-70 amending Lease L-16662 on Nov 18, 2025 (Port Commission minutes), and the memo (p.3) says the park covers approximately 2 acres with approximately 0.4 acre on the Port premises; the '~1.6 acres' on Power Station land in the log above is our own subtraction, not a sourced figure. (2) The log above says a Spring 2026 construction-pipeline document independently describes the project as a '2-acre Waterfront Park'; that document could not be located online or checked, so it should not be relied on. The '2-acre' size is supported by the Port memo instead. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, why_no_real_parcel, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- this polygon combines two different sourcing methods (see digitization_method) and has not been independently re-verified as a whole against satellite imagery. Its west edge is exact (shared vertices with Block 4/Humboldt Street Plaza/Block 9). Its east/shoreline edge inherits whatever accuracy Waterfront Park's own trace has -- treat it as a reasonable but not freshly-verified approximation of the real shoreline. This is the 'Power Station sub-area' complement to 'Prequel Park (Port sub-area)' -- together they approximate the full ~2-acre interim park project, though the true internal boundary between Port and Power-Station land has not been independently confirmed. The ~2-acre figure is stated in the Port Commission memo of Nov 14, 2025 (Calendar Item 10A, p.3: Prequel Park 'will cover approximately 2 acres, of which approximately .4 acres will be located on the Premises'); the press gives 2.5-2.75 acres.'; why_no_real_parcel: 'Open space with no subdivided Assessor parcel of its own within the largely unaddressed former power-station site. (This is our own parcel-search narration, not something any cited source establishes.)'; notes: 'Newly added 2026-09-16 to complement 'Prequel Park (Port sub-area)' -- see accuracy_caveat.'.

properties.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outlines; not tied to an Assessor parcel), cross-confirmed against ESRI World Imagery satellite tiles. This replaced, on 2026-09-17, a long chain of diagram- and text-based approximations (their sources are kept below for history). How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record). Originally three converging real-world sources: (1) 2011 Port RFI "Pier 70 Preferred Master Plan" map (sfport.com/sites/default/files/FileCenter/Documents/939-Pier70_RFI_3-2-11_web.pdf, PDF p.11), a scaled map with real street labels (Illinois St, 20th St) showing Building 21 immediately adjacent to Building 12 near the historic core, annotated "BUILDING 21 PROPOSED TO BE RELOCATED"; (2) Aug 3 2017 Port Commission memo (sfport.com/sites/default/files/Commission/Item%2011A%20Pier%2070%20Final.pdf, Exhibit F p.68): "Building 21 (Substation No. 5)... would be relocated approximately 75 feet to the southeast, and in its new location it would front Slipways Commons... sits directly next to the proposed new waterfront arts facility" (future tense: a planned relocation as part of the rehabilitation); (3) D4D Figure 3.6.1 "Illustrative Slipways Commons Plan" (p.56/PDF p.72), a scaled plan with a real 0-50-100ft bar and "MARYLAND ST" label, captioned "the historic node of Buildings 2, 12, and 21."
properties.digitization_method: REFIT 2026-09-13 with src/block_fit.py, on top of two prior corrections. (1) THIS PROJECT'S OWN real Building 12 anchor was wrong: status.csv had Building 12 joined to blklot 4045017 (700 Illinois St), an unrelated residential condo building over 500m from the real Building 12 -- corrected to 1070 Maryland St, blklot 4114010; see status.csv. (2) After correcting the anchor, this polygon (and Elevation Sky Park) was placed as a hand-computed offset rectangle, and a user screenshot showed it still crossing a real street -- the hand-computed street setbacks were not reliable. Replaced with a repeatable tool instead of a third hand computation: src/fetch_streets.py fetches real OSM street centerlines for the whole project area once (cached to data/raw/streets.geojson), and src/block_fit.py polygonizes them (plus the Port jurisdiction boundary, for shoreline-bounded blocks) into real block polygons, then fits a box of the requested size inside the correct one -- checked programmatically against every nearby street, not eyeballed. This building's real block (Maryland/21st/22nd St, the same one Elevation Sky Park occupies) is a real, well-formed small block, so block_fit.py fit it at its full documented 101ft x 75ft size, no shrinking needed, in the southern part of that block (nearer Building 12/22nd St); Elevation Sky Park occupies the rest of the same block to its north/east. ROTATED 2026-09-13: block_fit.py's earlier version always produced a true-north-aligned box, which looked visibly wrong once rendered -- this area's real street grid (Maryland/Louisiana/Delaware St etc.) is rotated relative to true north, and an axis-aligned box in a rotated block wastes space and doesn't match its neighbors' orientation. fit_box now rotates the box to match the bearing of the nearest real street segment before fitting/shrinking it. OVERLAP NOTE 2026-09-14 (project-wide overlap audit, SUPERSEDED 2026-09-16, see below): Fully overlapped Pier 70 Parcel E2 at the time -- expected given this marker's own low-confidence, directional-only placement; not clipped, since doing so would erase the marker entirely rather than usefully correct it. RE-TRACED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 deep pass, after applying Potrero's GCP-validation lessons to Pier 70's own transform): rather than continue relying on block_fit.py's street-polygon-fit approach (which only guarantees this box sits somewhere inside the right real block, not at a source-verified position), went back to the same source diagram used for this site's numbered parcels -- Figure 6.4.2 (Building Height Maximum), which shows Building 21 directly as one of its labeled gray 'Historic Buildings' boxes -- and pixel-traced its box directly (programmatic pixel-color sampling to find the box's true edges, at x=1551-1651, y=833-909 in the 2376x1836px source image, after an initial visual estimate proved off by ~55-60px on a badly-scaled crop). Converted via this site's validated 6-point affine transform (the same one used for Parcels A-H, residual error 1-8m against 5 real street intersections plus Building 12's real Assessor centroid) -- NOT block_fit.py's separate street-polygonize method. Cross-checked the transform itself against Building 12's real centroid (blklot 4114010) before trusting this result, per the lesson learned from Potrero's mis-measured-GCP incident: the transform reproduces Building 12's real-world position acceptably well, so it is not grossly miscalibrated. RESULT (2026-09-16, later superseded -- see below): this diagram-derived position was initially found to overlap Pier 70 Parcel E1 by 429.8 m2. FALSE ALARM, RESOLVED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 systematic feature-by-feature pass, later same day): a user-flagged visual check found E1's own traced shape was badly wrong (a misshapen quadrilateral that cut through this very '21' box and the open space beyond it, rather than the real L-shaped 90ft/65ft footprint shown on Figure 6.4.2). E1 was re-traced programmatically from its own two legend colors -- see pier70_e1.geojson's digitization_method -- and the overlap with this file dropped to exactly 0 m2, confirming Building 21's own position here was correct all along; the earlier overlap was entirely an artifact of E1's bad shape. Still overlapped 'Elevation Sky Park' by 275 m2 (unaffected by the E1 fix) -- see accuracy_caveat. RESOLVED 2026-09-17: that separate ESP entry was merged into Pier 70 Parcel E3's own row per an explicit user decision (see pier70_e3.geojson) and is no longer plotted as its own block, so this overlap no longer applies -- kept here for history. UPGRADED TO REAL FOOTPRINT 2026-09-17 (user request: 'building 21 can be more precise by leveraging satellite image, since it's an existing building that will remain'): rather than keep tracing/re-fitting a hand-drawn box, searched DataSF's Building Footprints dataset for real structures near this site (mblr=SF4052001 -- the same giant, largely-unsubdivided Assessor lot found to underlie much of central Pier 70, also covering Building 14; see status.csv's 4052001 row) and rendered all of them directly over ESRI World Imagery satellite tiles. That rendering showed two real, adjacent dark-roofed structures (367.8 and 367.2 sq m, combined 734.96 sq m / ~7,911 sqft) sitting almost exactly under this file's own previously-committed diagram-derived box -- a close match (within 4.4%) to the previously-cited 101ft x 75ft (~703.7 sq m) footprint size. A third, larger nearby footprint (1,879.7 sq m) that a pure diagram-position guess had initially favored turned out, on the satellite image, to actually be a paved section of Maryland St itself (a street mistakenly captured as a 'building' in the source dataset) -- not a structure at all; ruled out once seen against real imagery, exactly the kind of error satellite cross-checking is meant to catch. A small adjacent 49 sq m footprint sits ~9m south of the two main pieces (not touching) -- possibly a small appendage or a separate utility structure; not confirmed, so not included. Replaced the hand-traced diagram box with the union of the two matched real footprints (MultiPolygon, since DataSF's extraction has them as two separate touching-but-unmerged pieces). Checked for overlap against E1, E3, E4, Parcel D, Building 2, and Building 12's real parcel -- zero overlap with all of them at this corrected, smaller, more precisely-positioned footprint. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: (a) The Assessor parcels named above for Building 12 (blklot 4114010, 1070 Maryland St) and for the wrong earlier join (blklot 4045017, listed by DataSF at 700 Illinois St) come from DataSF's Assessor parcels (repo copy data/raw/parcels.geojson) and status.csv, not from the URLs cited in this file; the earlier description of 4045017 as an 'unrelated residential condo building' more than 500 m away is our own observation, not a sourced fact. (b) The footprint areas (367.8 and 367.2 sq m; a 1,879.7 sq m 'building' that is paved Maryland St) and the legacy lot id mblr SF4052001 are from DataSF Building Footprints (repo copy data/raw/buildings.geojson), a dataset not listed in source_doc_urls; the satellite reading is our own judgement. Lot 4052001 was retired on 2018-10-02 (DataSF Assessor parcels, acdm-wktn), so the earlier statements here that Building 21 'sits on' it describe a legacy id, not a current lot; the repo's parcel layer shows the footprint under active lot 4052009 (no street address). (c) The 2011 Port RFI map note 'BUILDING 21 PROPOSED TO BE RELOCATED' was re-read on PDF p.11 of the RFI, and the Aug 3, 2017 Port memo passage (Exhibit F, printed p.68) was re-read; both describe a proposed relocation, not a completed one, and both URLs are now listed in source_doc_urls. properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-17. China Basin Park (the Design Controls' name; 'Mission Rock Park' in the 2012 proposal) opened April 2024 with Phase 1 (sfyimby.com, 2024-04-26). Its real Assessor lot is 8719A005: 18,975 m2 / 4.69 ac, created when Seawall Lot 337 was subdivided in 2020. That lot still includes a 139 x 143 ft lobe south of the park's recorded south line, between the Bridgeview paseo lot 8719A007 and the TAFB lot 8719A003, which is exactly Block K's site (the Figure 6.2 trace of K lands on the lobe's four corners within 0.7-1.3 m; see mission_rock_block_k.geojson) and reads as paved staging on satellite imagery, not park. properties.digitization_method: REDONE 2026-09-14: the previous version of this polygon was traced using a transform fit from 5 street intersections plus Historic Building 12's real footprint as a 6th anchor. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. RE-TRACED 2026-09-16 (full Pier 70 geometry restart, after a systematic pass found 9 of this site's other 'trusted' parcels were meaningfully wrong): re-measured programmatically instead of by eye, for consistency with the rest of this site -- isolated this legend color (RGB [128,193,219]) and extracted a clean rectangular contour (OpenCV) at pixel (1203,437)-(1401,682). Converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. Result is close to (within ~5m of) the prior hand-read version -- this parcel's own corners were already read correctly; kept for methodological consistency across the site. Still overlaps 'Noonan Building' by ~2843 m2 -- an already-documented, expected overlap given Noonan's own low-confidence, directional-only placement. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the 'Building 14 footprint' identified by blklot 4052001 refers to a legacy lot id: DataSF Building Footprints carry mblr SF4052001 on 21 footprints in the repo copy (data/raw/buildings.geojson), the data do not show which is Building 14, and blklot 4052001 was retired on 2018-10-02 (DataSF Assessor parcels, acdm-wktn), so it is not a current Assessor lot. No outside source is cited for that identification. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built (Port Item 11A, Aug 2026: the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'), and no source read ties it to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor parcels include new lots created for the 28-acre district in 2019, without street addresses, but which lot (if any) is Parcel A's was not established. It currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district. Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. EXTENDED SOUTH 2026-09-17 (user-flagged): this block's south edge fell ~11m short of the real sidewalk visible in satellite imagery, leaving a strip of unclaimed vacant land between the block and the street -- consistent with this site's known local scale error for parcels far from the transform's Illinois/Michigan St anchors (see Parcel E1's digitization_method for the same root cause). The diagram itself (Figure 6.4.2) shows this block's fill running right up to the street with no setback, so extended the two south vertices by 11m (measured via satellite pixel-color transition to the real sidewalk, 3 sample transects) to close the gap, matching the diagram's own convention rather than re-deriving the whole transform.'; notes: 'Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see accuracy_caveat.'.

Since this plaza was defined to share PKN's exact x-range by construction, it inherited both problems. Corrected to match PKN's newly-retraced, correct-resolution contour exactly: x 389-578 (PKN's real east-west extent), y 371-440 (440 = PKN's corrected north edge, matched exactly so the shared boundary still can't overlap; 371 = 401/1.08, rescaling the south-boundary-line pixel reading since it comes from Figure 3.3.1, not 6.4.2, and there is no independent legend-color fill to re-detect there). properties.project_name: Pier 70 Waterfront Open Space (Waterfront Terrace / Slipways Commons / Waterfront Promenade / Pier 70 Shoreline) -- combined, approximate
properties.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155); named/numbered per Figure 3.4.1 - Overview of Public Spaces (p.52).
properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 systematic feature-by-feature pass): the D4D names four separate open spaces along this site's waterfront -- Waterfront Terrace (Fig 3.4.1 zone 1, near Parcel B), Slipways Commons (zone 2, the plaza between E1/E4 and E2/E3), Waterfront Promenade (zone 3, the shoreline path), and Pier 70 Shoreline (zone 4, near the point north of E4) -- but Figure 3.4.1 itself (and Figure 6.4.2's own 'Public Open Space' fill, used here) renders all four as ONE continuous, undivided green area with no internal boundary line drawn anywhere between them. Rather than fabricate a specific dividing line that no source shows, this is tracked as one combined feature covering all four. Traced via programmatic pixel-color detection (isolating Figure 6.4.2's 'Public Open Space' fill color, RGB [194,218,106], with morphological closing to bridge small text/icon gaps, then an OpenCV contour extraction simplified to ~35 vertices) rather than hand-clicking, since this is a long, irregularly-shaped (and intentionally jagged/riprap-shore-like, per the diagram's own hatching) strip. Converted via this site's validated 6-point affine transform. Clipped against Parcels E1, E4, E3, and H2's own already-committed geometries via shapely difference() (the raw pixel trace overlapped each by a small amount, and building parcels take priority over this open-space trace) -- this produced a MultiPolygon with one large piece (~3.0 acres) and a smaller ~0.23-acre piece separated by H2. NOT clipped against Building 21 or Elevation Sky Park (this site's own already-acknowledged low-confidence markers) for the same reason those aren't clipped against E1-E4 elsewhere in this dataset. GAP FILLED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged): a ~31m gap existed directly east of Parcel E3 -- this polygon's two pieces each nearly touched E3 near its NW and SW corners (per the earlier clip against E1/E4/E3/H2) but nothing filled the shoreline strip along E3's own east edge in between, even though Figure 6.4.2 shows this whole shoreline band as one continuous Public Open Space area with no break at E3. Added a connecting piece along E3's east edge, bounded on the east by the real Port Jurisdiction boundary (data/raw/port_jurisdiction.geojson, the same authoritative shoreline/bulkhead line already used elsewhere in this project) rather than an invented shoreline shape, and clipped against E3's current (2026-09-17, extended-south) geometry so it doesn't overlap it. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- notes: 'Newly added 2026-09-16 as part of a systematic pass adding this site's previously-untracked open space -- see accuracy_caveat for why this combines four named D4D spaces into one polygon.'.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE, AND KNOWINGLY UNSUBDIVIDED -- combines four D4D-named open spaces (Waterfront Terrace, Slipways Commons, Waterfront Promenade, Pier 70 Shoreline) into one polygon because the D4D figures used (3.4.1 and 6.4.2) show one continuous fill; the Port's SUD Land Use Plan (Exhibit A4-1, 03/13/2018) labels separate 'Open Space Segments' (WTP, SC-1, SC-2, WP-1, WP-2), which this polygon does not follow; do not treat this as a single named place. Total traced area (~4.0-4.3 acres before/after clipping) is a reasonable match to the D4D's own combined figures (a ~5.0-acre waterfront area covering the first three, plus part of a ~1,300-linear-foot shoreline) but is not a precise subdivision or survey. Programmatically traced from a diagram's fill color, not hand-verified vertex-by-vertex.

properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-17 in response to a user-caught gap: this project's whole open-space network for Pier 70 (Figure 3.4.1, p.52) lists 8 named zones, but only 6 had been traced -- Irish Hill Playground (zone 8, ~2.0 acres per the D4D text, 'an open space adjacent to the existing remnant of Irish Hill') and Irish Hill Corner Plaza (zone 7, no acreage given) were missing entirely. FIRST PASS: traced the green 'Public Open Space' fill (RGB [194,218,106]) directly from Figure 6.4.2's pixels, then clipped it against PKS/HDY3/C1/C2/HDY1-2's own committed geometries -- this ceded roughly 45% of the raw trace back to those neighbors and left an underestimate (~0.68 acres) that didn't visually touch several of the surrounding parcels. SECOND PASS same day: switched to the real, street-polygonized block (src/block_fit.py) bounded by Illinois St and 22nd St, unioned with PKS/HDY3/C1/C2/HDY1-2's own geometries, minus those same 5 parcels -- fixed the touching problem for PKS/HDY3/HDY1-2 but the user caught two remaining defects: it still had small (2.5m and 9.8m) gaps against C1 and C2 (the real street-block polygon's own edges don't line up exactly with C1/C2's independently-traced boundaries), and it incorrectly extended ~13m south of HDY1/2's own south edge (the real block reaches all the way to 22nd St's actual curb, which is slightly further south than HDY1/2's own, separately-traced south edge -- creating a sliver of 'phantom' park space south of a parcel that the diagram shows going straight to 22nd St). THIRD PASS: re-included the original diagram-traced raw contour (see first pass) in the union alongside the real block and the 5 parcels -- since that raw trace independently overlapped C1 by 1,142 sq m and C2 by 74 sq m, unioning it in extends the combined shape properly into contact with both (0m gap, confirmed) without the crude 'buffer everything outward' approach tried and rejected first (which fixed the C1/C2 gap but ballooned the total area to 3.3+ acres by reaching past C1/C2 in directions that had nothing to do with Irish Hill). Then explicitly clipped the whole result to never extend south of HDY1/2's own southernmost latitude, fixing the second defect directly rather than hoping the union wouldn't overreach. Also dropped one degenerate near-zero-area sliver piece (9e-6 sq m) left over from the boolean operations. Resulting area ~7,831 sq m (~1.94 acres). FOURTH PASS 2026-09-17 (streets/block-alignment review): PKS and HDY3 were both re-traced this same pass after a confirmed pixel-resolution bug moved them (see those files' digitization_method) -- HDY3 shifted to stay attached, but PKS moved further away, reopening a ~23m gap between this feature and PKS. The real, street-polygonized block (from the third pass) fell just 2.6m short of the newly-corrected PKS on its own -- a small, plausible real gap between the block-polygonization tool's edge and PKS's own diagram-traced edge, not the ~23m the raw union produced -- so the block polygon (only, not the parcels) was buffered outward by 6m before unioning, closing most of it; a residual 1.26m gap remains against PKS specifically, accepted as within this project's already-documented 5-15m trace precision rather than chased further with more buffering (which was tried at 15m earlier in this file's history and caused an unrelated overreach). Re-verified 0m distance / 0 overlap against HDY3, C1, C2, and HDY1/2, and 0 overlap with PKN and the 20th Street Plaza. Dropped a new degenerate sliver piece (~12 sq m) from this pass's boolean ops. Resulting area ~10,338 sq m (~2.55 acres) -- larger than the D4D's ~2.0-acre citation, mostly from the corrected PKS/HDY3 positions genuinely opening up more real space here than the earlier (buggy, too-far-south) PKS/HDY3 traces implied; not re-shrunk to hit the citation, since the citation was never used as a target, only a plausibility check. FIFTH PASS 2026-09-17 (REPLACED, user-flagged 'Irish Hill Playground seems misplaced'): the block_fit/union approach above was abandoned entirely. Looking at the actual diagram again, this green area is not just 'whatever real block Irish Hill roughly sits near' -- Figure 6.4.2 draws its exact boundary directly, including the hill's own contour-line hatching. Re-traced it the same way Waterfront Open Space was traced: isolated the 'Public Open Space' fill color (RGB [194,218,106]) in a crop covering the PKS/HDY3/C1/C2/HDY1-2 area, morphological close+open to bridge hatching/text gaps, OpenCV contour extraction (simplified to 15 vertices), converted via the validated 6-point affine transform. This raw trace overlapped HDY3/HDY1-2/C1/C2 by small amounts (each block's own black border stroke sits a couple pixels inside where the flat green fill visually ends), so it was clipped via shapely difference() against all four of those committed geometries -- same pattern as Waterfront Open Space's own clip against E1/E4/E3/H2. While investigating the C1 overlap specifically, found C1 itself carried the same 2376x1836-vs-2200x1700 resolution-mismatch bug already fixed on PKN/PKS/HDY3 (see pier70_c1.geojson's digitization_method) -- its true south edge is ~26m further north than previously recorded, which had been silently eating into this exact area. Fixed C1 first, then re-ran this clip. Result: 0m gap/overlap against HDY3, HDY1/2, and C2; 0.9m gap against the corrected C1 (within normal trace precision); the ~23m distance to PKS is NOT a gap to close -- the diagram shows PKS separated from this open space by the full width of HDY3, they were never meant to touch. This new trace does NOT surround HDY1/2 (no interior hole) -- the diagram simply doesn't show Irish Hill wrapping around it; the previous approach's 'surrounds on 3 sides' shape was an artifact of the block-fit/union method, not something Figure 6.4.2 actually draws. Area ~4,862 sq m (~1.20 acres), smaller than the D4D's ~2.0-acre citation -- as with the citation-vs-trace gaps already documented elsewhere in this project (e.g. Mission Rock Square), the citation is treated as a plausibility check, not a target; matching what the diagram itself draws, and touching real neighboring parcels correctly, takes priority. RE-CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (same day): C1 itself was found to be significantly mispositioned (overlapping the real 21st St by over 100m of its length -- see pier70_c1.geojson) and was moved south by ~28-31m to ground-truth against the real street. Re-ran this file's own clip against C1's corrected position; area dropped further to ~3,249 sq m (~0.80 acres). Confirmed 0m gap/overlap against HDY3, HDY1/2, C1, and C2. EXEMPTED FROM STREET CLIPPING 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: shape looked disproportionate/weird, 'as if leaving room for an expansion of Michigan street south which is nowhere in drawing'): exactly right -- Michigan St's real centerline (CNN 8999000) runs through this feature's own interior (same segment found splitting HDY1/2 into two pieces, see that file's digitization_method), and join_approximate.py's auto-clip was silently cutting this feature into a MultiPolygon around it (raw 3,249 sq m -> processed 2,782 sq m, a real but not obviously 'major' percentage that still produced a visibly wrong disconnected shape). Figure 6.4.2 draws this as one continuous green space with no street through it. Exempted from street clipping for the same reason as HDY1/2: this ambiguous, likely-informal site track (not a real curbed street at this latitude) shouldn't carve up a planned open space the diagram shows as whole. RE-TRACED 2026-09-17 (same day, user-flagged: 'the diagonal between HDY buildings seems disproportionate compared to HDY3'): correct -- overlaying the raw color-mask trace directly on page171.png showed a spurious deep V-shaped spike cutting into the middle of the green area, with no corresponding line or color break in the diagram at all (the green fill is fully continuous there). Root cause: a small tree/planting icon drawn within the green space broke the color mask into two blobs that a too-small morphological closing kernel (13px) bridged incorrectly, inventing a notch neither the diagram nor any real feature shows. Re-extracted with a larger closing kernel (25px, still small relative to the icon-to-real-boundary distance) to bridge the icon gap correctly; the resulting shape follows HDY3's own diagonal edge much more closely, with only a small, shallow, plausible dent remaining (matching a slightly darker hatching band visible in the diagram alongside HDY3's slope, not a hard error). Re-clipped against HDY3/HDY1-2/C1/C2; final area ~3,230 sq m (~0.80 acres, effectively unchanged from before -- this was a shape-accuracy fix, not a size fix). CHECKED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: 'should fill the space touching HYD3, HYD1/2, C1/C2, and 21st street'): re-verified this feature's touching relationships directly -- confirmed 0m gap/overlap against C1, C2, and HDY3, and a 3.7m gap against HDY1/2 and PKS (both within this project's already-documented 5-15m trace precision, not a real gap to close). The 'and 21st street' part does not hold as a literal requirement: this feature does not (and per the diagram should not) touch 21st St directly -- Parcel C1 (west portion) and Parcel K South (PKS, further west) occupy the FULL frontage between this open space and 21st St along this feature's entire north edge, confirmed by checking that C1's own north edge (ground-truthed against the real 21st St curb line) sits ~26-38m further north than this feature's own northernmost point, with no gap in that C1/PKS wall for this feature to reach through. This matches Figure 6.4.2, which draws Irish Hill Playground one row south of the C1/PKS/21st-St row, not fronting the street itself. RE-TRACED 2026-09-17 (same day, after PKN/PKS/C1/HDY3 were restored to their pure diagram positions -- see those files -- following confirmation that the '21st St ground-truth shift' premise was wrong, a paper-street issue, not a planned relocation): re-did this feature's raw color trace with a taller crop (extending north to y=740 instead of stopping at y=850-890) to check whether the green 'Public Open Space' fill extends further north than previously captured. It does: the fill runs continuously from y=775 (the same row as PKS/C1's restored, true north edge -- i.e. immediately south of '21ST ST (NEW)' itself) down through this site's full extent, confirmed by direct pixel scans at x=560/590/620 (the gap between PKS/HDY3's east edge and C1's west edge) showing the green fill starting at y=775-776 with no other color in between. This matches the user's own read of the diagram: this open space fills the space between PKS, C1, and 21st St. Extracted via the same method as before (isolate RGB [194,218,106], 25px morphological close+open, OpenCV contour), producing a 12-vertex main contour plus a separate ~158 sq m piece near Illinois St/HDY3's SW corner (the Irish Hill Corner Plaza zone). Clipped via shapely difference() against the restored PKS/HDY3/C1 and the separately-corrected C2 (see that file), plus HDY1/2 (unchanged). Result is a MultiPolygon: main piece ~6,299 sq m, corner piece ~158 sq m, total ~6,458 sq m (~1.60 acres). Confirmed within 1-1.6m (normal trace precision) of PKS, HDY3, C1, and C2, and 0.06m of HDY1/2. RE-CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (same day, after C1 was independently clipped against the real Building 113-116 footprint -- see that file -- shrinking it slightly from its pure-diagram size): re-ran this feature's own clip against C1's updated shape. Total area now ~6,458 sq m (effectively unchanged, C1's own change was on its north side, away from this shared boundary). RE-CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (same day, after PKN/PKS/C1/C2/HDY3/HDY1-2 were all repositioned against the corrected, real-anchored '21st St (NEW)' line and HDY3/HDY1-2 were both extended to the real 22nd St curb -- see those files): re-ran this feature's own raw diagram color-trace against all six updated neighbor positions. Total area drops from ~6,458 to ~4,258 sq m (main piece ~4,138 + corner piece ~120), mostly because HDY1/2's own growth (extending to the real 22nd St curb) now consumes much of what was previously open space south of HDY3. Confirmed touching (0-3.5m gaps, within normal trace precision) against HDY3, PKS, C1, C2, and HDY1/2. RE-CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (same pass, found via check_geometry_quality.py): also overlapped the repositioned (grown-south) PKN by 72 sq m along this feature's own north edge -- clipped that too. Final area ~4,186 sq m total (main ~4,066 + corner ~120). RE-CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (same pass as HDY3/HDY1-2/C2/PKN adjustments above): found this feature's own north edge crossed to the NORTH side of the '21st St (NEW)' reference line (data/manual/pier70_21st_street.geojson) by up to ~20m -- the raw diagram trace's own northern extent (unchanged since it was first color-extracted) was never re-clipped after PKS/C1 moved south in the prior round, since it had stopped overlapping them entirely. Added an explicit clip against a half-plane north of the '21st St (NEW)' line, plus re-clipped against the now-touching HDY3/HDY1-2 and the grown PKN. Area now ~3,673 sq m (main ~3,552 + corner ~120). RE-CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (same pass as HDY3/HDY1-2's redesign): with a real gap restored between HDY3 and HDY1/2 (see those files), this feature now fills that corridor down toward 22nd St, reconnecting into a single polygon (the separate ~120 sq m 'corner plaza' sliver from the prior round merges into the main body through this corridor). Area now ~2,615 sq m. Confirmed 0-5m gaps (normal trace precision) against all six neighbors. RE-CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (same day, after HDY3 and HDY1/2 were rebuilt a second time from the user's own hand-drawn sketch -- see those files' digitization_method): re-ran this feature's own clip against both blocks' new shapes. HDY3 now reaches further into this corridor than the previous round (322 sq m new overlap), HDY1/2 pulled back and no longer overlaps this feature at all (0 sq m, was already 0). Area now ~2,293 sq m, still a single Polygon (no fragmentation) and still 0m gap/overlap against C1, C2, PKS, and PKN. REBUILT 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: 'playground should fill the spaces between buildings as shown in drawing'): abandoned the raw-diagram-color-trace-plus-clip approach entirely (it had been producing a string of small, repeatedly-drifting gaps against one neighbor or another every time any neighbor moved, since the trace's own boundary was never actually defined IN TERMS OF those neighbors' edges). Rebuilt this feature directly as the walk around its neighbors' own already-committed boundaries, so it touches all of them by construction rather than by incidental proximity: HDY3's own NE corner (shared with PKS) -> C1's own SW and SE corners (its south edge) -> C2's own NE and NW corners (its north and west edges) -> HDY1/2's own NE corner (v1) and its newly-recomputed north corner (v0, see that file) -> HDY3's own corridor point -> close. Every edge of this polygon except one (the short HDY3_NE-to-C1_SW gap-filler, ~7m, since those two blocks don't quite touch) is now an EXACT shared boundary (0m gap by construction, not by measurement) with a real neighboring parcel. Area drops from ~2,293 to ~1,888 sq m, mostly because HDY1/2's own north corner moved east/north (see that file's own parallel-edge fix), shrinking the gap it leaves for this feature to fill. REBUILT AGAIN 2026-09-17 (same day, user-flagged with a hand-drawn overlay on the rendered map: 'playground should fill the spaces between buildings as shown in drawing... where I see the color missing'): the rebuild above only walked the 'upper gap' (C1/C2 vs the HDY3/HDY1-2 row) and left three real, satellite-visible open areas uncovered, all confirmed against the user's own marked-up screenshot (digitized via the same ORB-feature-matching + marker-calibration pipeline used for HDY3/HDY1-2's own hand sketch): (1) the HDY3-to-HDY1/2 CORRIDOR itself, from the shared top corner down to near 22nd St, was never actually added to this feature after being carved out as a gap between those two blocks -- added it back as the quadrilateral bounded by HDY3's own corridor edge (D to its 22nd-St/SW corner) and HDY1/2's own corridor edge (v0 to v3), which are parallel by construction (see those files). (2) A real, ~15-18m gap between HDY1/2's own east edge (v1-v2) and C2's own west edge (v0-v1/SW) -- the two blocks' side-by-side edges never actually touch -- confirmed geometrically (not just from the user's sketch) by comparing their longitudes directly. Added as the strip between them. (3) A smaller gap on the WEST side of C1 (between C1's own west edge and PKS's own east edge/the HDY3-PKS shared corner), which the user's sketch marked as a distinct notch reaching further north than this feature's previous extent -- taken directly from the user's own traced coordinates (no clean existing-polygon edges define this one), then clipped via shapely difference() against C1 and PKS since the raw traced notch initially overlapped both by a modest amount. All three additions unioned into one shape (still a single simple Polygon, not a MultiPolygon) and simplified to drop redundant near-duplicate vertices from the boolean ops. Re-verified: 0 overlap with HDY1/2, C1, C2, and PKS; a negligible ~1 sq m residual against HDY3 (rounding from the simplify step, not a real encroachment). Area grows from ~1,888 to ~4,236 sq m. CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (same day, user-flagged again: 'you left out part of the space between PKS and C1'): root cause of the shortfall -- the notch above was clipped against C1's RAW, pre-street-clip geometry (data/manual/pier70_c1.geojson), which is NOT what actually renders on the map. C1 itself loses ~15m off its own west edge to a real-street clip in join_approximate.py (documented in that file's own digitization_method as '11.7% of this block's area... in the buffered real-street layer'), so the ACTUAL rendered C1 sits well east of its own raw west edge. Clipping this feature's notch against the raw file made it discard ~466 sq m that is genuinely open (uncolored) on the rendered map, not actually inside C1 at all -- confirmed by pixel-sampling the rendered PNG directly and by comparing against C1's own post-clip geometry in data/processed/approximate_projects.geojson (whose west edge sits at -122.38634 to -122.38637, ~15m east of the raw file's -122.38652). Re-clipped the notch against C1's PROCESSED shape instead (now a negligible ~3 sq m residual) while keeping the PKS clip (PKS isn't meaningfully street-clipped, so its raw and processed shapes already agree). Also swapped this feature's own touching point on C1's south edge from C1's raw SW corner to C1's actual post-clip corner, for the same reason. Re-verified 0 overlap against HDY1/2, C2, PKS, and C1's own processed shape. Area grows from ~4,236 to ~4,734 sq m -- this whole increase is the space that was wrongly ceded to C1's raw (non-rendered) footprint. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the earlier entry above saying Figure 6.4.2 draws Irish Hill Playground one row south of the C1/PKS/21st-St row, not fronting the street, was a misreading: on the rendered figure the green fill reaches 21st St between PKS and C1, as a later entry and the accuracy_caveat recognise. The earlier entry is kept as history. Nothing in the geometry was changed. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- traced directly from Figure 6.4.2's own 'Public Open Space' fill color (programmatic color-region contour extraction), then clipped against PKS/HDY3/C1/C2/HDY1-2's own committed geometries. Now extends north to touch '21ST ST (NEW)' directly in the gap between PKS and C1, matching the diagram's own drawn fill. The geometry is now a single Polygon: an earlier trace produced a separate small piece near Illinois St (the Irish Hill Corner Plaza zone), but it reconnects to the main body through the corridor between HDY3 and HDY1/2 (see digitization_method), and on the rendered Figure 6.4.2 the green band between HDY3 and HDY1/2 runs continuously to the Illinois/22nd corner.'; notes: 'Newly added 2026-09-17 as part of closing a gap the user pointed out: not all of Figure 3.4.1's 8 named open-space zones had been traced onto the map. Geometry redone multiple times the same day -- see digitization_method for the full history, including a full replacement after a user flagged this shape as looking misplaced.'.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- traced directly from Figure 6.4.2's own 'Public Open Space' fill color (outlined automatically by color), then trimmed to the mapped shapes of PKS, HDY3, C1, C2 and HDY1/2. Now extends north to touch '21ST ST (NEW)' directly in the gap between PKS and C1, matching the diagram's own drawn fill. The geometry is now a single Polygon: an earlier trace produced a separate small piece near Illinois St (the Irish Hill Corner Plaza zone), but it reconnects to the main body through the corridor between HDY3 and HDY1/2 (see the mapping log), and on the rendered Figure 6.4.2 the green band between HDY3 and HDY1/2 runs continuously to the Illinois/22nd corner. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
properties.why_no_real_parcel: Open space with no Assessor lot of its own identified. Port Item 9B (2017) lists Irish Hill Park among 'Port improvements outside of the 28-Acre Site' and as a 'Port or Hoedown Yard Vertical Developer obligation, at Port's discretion', so it is not within Brookfield's 28-acre site; the earlier statement that it is is withdrawn. Which Assessor lot(s) it lies on has not been checked.
properties.regulatory_context: Part of the Pier 70 D4D's Open Space Network (Section 3.4): Irish Hill Playground (Section 3.12, ~2.0 acres), described as an open space adjacent to the existing remnant of Irish Hill (Section 3.2) -- an approximately 35-foot tall serpentine outcropping, today approximately seven percent of what the hill once was (D4D Section 3.2); the National Register nomination says Building 12 (1941) was built on newly leveled ground where most of Irish Hill once stood. The D4D does not say when or how the rest was removed. Irish Hill Corner Plaza (Section 3.11) is a separate, smaller named zone at the southwest corner of this same open area, near the Illinois St/22nd St corner.
properties.notes: Added 2026-09-17, after it was found that not all of Figure 3.4.1's 8 named open-space zones had been traced onto the map. The shape was redrawn several times the same day, including a full replacement after it was found to look misplaced. The full history is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).

properties.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
properties.digitization_method: REDONE 2026-09-14: the previous version of this polygon was traced using a transform fit from 5 street intersections plus Historic Building 12's real footprint as a 6th anchor. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (second pass, same day): after the shear fix above, a user-flagged visual check still showed this block overlapping paved streets. Root cause found: several blocks (PKN, PKS, HDY3, HDY1/2, E4) had their OWN corner pixel positions misread during transcription -- e.g. PKN's west edge was recorded as pixel x=163 when the diagram's own gridline labels put it at x=355 (which is where the Illinois St anchor point itself was measured). This was a transcription slip, not a transform error -- the 6-point transform's anchors were unaffected (confirmed: A, B, C1, C2, D, E1, E2, E3, F/G, H1, H2 were read correctly the first time). Re-read all 5 affected blocks' corners directly against their crop images' own labeled gridlines and recomputed. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (sixth pass): user-flagged check found a real gap between PKN's south edge and PKS's own north edge -- both blocks were transformed/traced independently and didn't agree on where their shared internal boundary sits, leaving an ~8-11m strip of real, currently-parked-in pavement claimed by neither polygon. Fixed by setting PKS's north edge to exactly match PKN's (corrected) south edge, eliminating the gap. CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-09-14: the prior fix copied PKN's entire south edge onto PKS, but PKN is wider than PKS at that boundary, and this made PKS balloon east into a driveway/building area that isn't part of the real lot (confirmed visually, and by a jump from 5% to 22% clipped against the street buffer). Redone by keeping PKS's own original NW/NE longitudes (its real width) and only raising each corner's latitude to sit exactly on PKN's south edge line (linear interpolation, not a flat copy) -- closes the real gap without changing PKS's real east-west extent. CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-09-14 (seventh pass): user clarified the diagonal row of angled cars along this block's west side is curbside parking on Illinois Street itself, not part of the PKN/PKS parcel -- the earlier fixes had mistakenly extended the west edge to include it. Pulled the west edge back east to -122.3874, matching where the diagonal on-street parking row ends and the lot's own perpendicular-grid parking begins (visually distinct in the satellite image). CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-09-14 (eighth pass): PKS's diagonal on-street parking row sits further east than PKN's (its own separate measurement, not assumed identical) -- the shared -122.3874 value cut through the middle of PKS's diagonal row instead of clearing it. Re-measured PKS's own diagonal-row/white-separation-stripe transition directly and moved to -122.38733. REVERTED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 border-alignment audit): the sixth/seventh/eighth-pass satellite corrections above (matching this block's north/west edges to today's real parking-lot striping) were built on a mistaken premise -- this project maps the D4D's PLANNED layout against today's satellite imagery as a backdrop, not the other way around. Snapping this parcel's north edge to PKN's satellite-corrected south edge erased '21ST ST (NEW)' entirely, a real, deliberately-labeled future street Figure 6.4.2 draws with its own paved width between PKN and PKS. Re-traced this block directly from the diagram instead: programmatic pixel-color detection (isolating this legend color, RGB [169,143,173]) found this block's own purple fill spans pixel x 374-591, y 825-927 in the 2376x1836 source image (y=825 is just south of 21ST ST (NEW)'s drawn width; y=927 is this block's own south edge/border with HDY3, which is unchanged and still lines up with HDY3's north edge) -- converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform used for this site's other numbered parcels. This restores the diagram's own street gap between PKN and PKS (now ~19-26m, consistent with a real street width) that the satellite-snapping passes had collapsed to zero, and also corrects this block's east edge, which the satellite passes had measured ~40-50m narrower than the diagram shows (the block extends east to a real open-space area before Parcel C1, not stopping at the on-street parking columns those passes were tracing). The satellite-based lessons above (curbside-parking exclusion, sidewalk-color detection) remain useful technique notes for tracing REAL/existing features elsewhere in this project, but do not apply to this PLANNED parcel's own boundary. Also corrected this block's south edge (its internal division with HDY3, not a real street) from pixel y~986-992 to y~927 -- a plain diagram-corner-misread, unrelated to the satellite-vs-plan issue above: two independent grid-overlay crops of Figure 6.4.2 confirmed the true PKS/HDY3 divider line sits at y~929-931, ~55-60px north of where this file previously had it. HDY3's own north edge is being corrected to match in the same pass (see that file). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. CORRECTED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 systematic feature-by-feature pass): a batch color-region check found this block's committed shape extended too far south (into the Irish Hill Playground green space) and not far enough east, versus the diagram's actual fill. Re-measured programmatically instead of by eye: isolated this legend color (RGB [128,193,219]) in a crop spanning this block's 3 internal sub-division cells, merged them (morphological closing across the thin cell-divider lines), and extracted the outer contour (OpenCV) -- a clean rectangle at pixel (698,838)-(1075,957). Converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. Confirmed zero overlap with PKS, C2, or HDY1/2. RESOLVED 2026-09-16 (same day, full geometry restart): the 'Pier 70 Building 2 (Warehouse No. 2)' overlap mentioned in this file's own accuracy_caveat no longer applies -- Building 2 was found to be badly mislocated (a west-side vacant lot, not its real east-cluster position next to Buildings 12 and 21) and has been relocated; it no longer overlaps this parcel at all. See that file's own digitization_method. CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (found while investigating a user-flagged Irish Hill Playground misplacement): the 2026-09-16 pixel bbox above (698,838)-(1075,957) turns out to be the SAME confirmed 2376x1836-vs-2200x1700 resolution-mismatch bug already found and fixed on PKN/PKS/HDY3 that same day -- dividing each value by 1.08 (698/1.08=646.3, 838/1.08=776.9, 1075/1.08=995.4, 957/1.08=886.1) lands almost exactly on a fresh, independent color-fill extraction on page171.png at its correct 2200x1700 resolution: (647,776)-(996,887). This block was evidently never rechecked when that bug was fixed elsewhere. Re-measured via the same method (isolate RGB [128,193,219], morphological closing across the 3 internal cell dividers, OpenCV outer contour) directly on page171.png and converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. New shape is a plain rectangle, confirmed 0 overlap with PKS, HDY3, or C2 (33-39m clearance to each) and used to correct the previously-wrong Irish Hill Playground clip boundary (see that file's own digitization_method). CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: 'C1 now is cut by 21st street when it should just be south of it'): the fix above was itself wrong -- both it AND the pre-existing committed geometry it replaced overlapped the real, confirmed 21st St centerline (CNN 15233000) by well over 100m of its length (145.7m for the old version, 128.9m for the resolution-bug fix), i.e. this was never actually a resolution-scaling problem for this specific edge, and fixing the resolution bug alone did not fix the real issue. Root cause: this diagram-transform, even correctly applied, places this row of blocks (C1's own latitude band, roughly midway between the transform's Illinois/Michigan St anchors and its more-distant east side) measurably too far north relative to where the real street actually is -- PKS, immediately to this block's west and fronting the same stretch of 21st St, sits with 0 overlap against this same street segment, so the discrepancy is specific to this eastern extension of the row, not a sitewide bias. Rather than patch the transform, ground-truthed this block's own north edge directly against the real street centerline (the same one PKS already sits correctly against): computed the real centerline's latitude at each of this block's own longitudes (linear interpolation along CNN 15233000, which is nearly straight over this span) and set this block's north edge 6.8m south of it (this project's own empirically-measured real curb-to-centerline half-width -- see street_geometry.py), then shifted the two south corners by the same amount to preserve the block's shape/depth from the diagram. Confirmed 0 overlap with 21st St, Michigan St's own north-south segment (8999001), and Building 113-116's real footprint; 11.7% of this block's area now falls in the buffered real-street layer (a normal corner-lot-style sliver along Michigan St's separate north-south alignment near this block's west edge, well under this project's 15% flag threshold), down from 45%. This move also required re-clipping Irish Hill Playground, which had been clipped against this block's previous (wrong) position -- see that file's own digitization_method. RE-INVESTIGATED 2026-09-17 (yet again, same day, after user feedback called the prior revert-and-redo cycle 'mostly a downgrade' and asked for a clarifying question rather than another guess): went back to first principles instead of more pixel geometry. Two checks, both requested by the user: (1) searched the D4D's own text (Section 4.11, Specific Streets Design Intent) for any description of 21st St being relocated or realigned -- found none; it describes 21st St as 'primarily serves as an alley from Illinois Street to the waterfront,' with no mention of a moved alignment. (2) Pulled real satellite imagery (src/satellite_check.py) directly over where DataSF's official centerline (CNN 15232000/15233000) says 21st St runs between Illinois and Michigan St -- it shows vegetation, graded dirt, a tree, and a vehicle-storage yard: zero pavement. So the earlier 'the D4D relocates 21st St' theory (this file's own prior REVERTED/RETRACTED entries) was an overreach from a real but simpler fact: DataSF's centerline here is a paper (platted, unbuilt) alignment, the same failure mode as three other already-excluded CNNs in street_geometry.py (12915000, 15200000, 15228000) -- not a deliberate relocation. Added CNN 15232000/15233000 to that same exclusion list, with the satellite evidence documented there. User's explicit instruction: note that this stretch of 21st St isn't built yet, but for this map's purpose (showing the planned FUTURE parcel state) treat the diagram's own drawn '21ST ST (NEW)' position as authoritative. Restored this block to its pure diagram-transform position accordingly -- the same value already found and confirmed multiple times this project (most recently before the mistaken ground-truth shift below). This restored position again overlaps the real Building 113-116 footprint (~1015 sq m) -- re-added to check_geometry_quality.py's EXPECTED_OVERLAP_PAIRS. Whether that specific overlap is itself correct is flagged for a visual check against the rendered map before treating it as settled. RECONSIDERED 2026-09-17 (same day, before treating the ~1015 sq m overlap with real Building 113-116 as expected): checked the D4D text itself (Section 1.3, Figure 1.3.3 legend) for that building's actual fate rather than assuming a demolition -- it lists Building 113-116 as one of the 'Historic Buildings to be Rehabilitated' (kept, not demolished), part of the National Register-listed UIW Historic District. That rules out the 'planned demolition, overlap is expected' reasoning already used elsewhere on this site for buildings that ARE slated for removal. Since Building 113-116's own footprint is real/surveyed (high confidence) and this block's own boundary is diagram-transform-derived (5-15m tolerance), clipped this block against the real building footprint via shapely difference() rather than accepting the overlap -- area drops from ~3,730 to ~2,701 sq m. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. OVERLAP FIX 2026-09-14: a project-wide overlap audit found this block spatially overlapping Potrero Power Station Block 3/4 in real-world coordinates near the two sites' shared border -- a genuine disagreement between Pier 70's and Potrero's independent transforms, not a same-site priority call. Clipped back from Potrero's blocks, since Potrero's transform was independently validated against real building bearings (Sophie Maxwell/UCSF) earlier in this project, while this specific southern edge of Pier 70 has not been satellite-verified. CORRECTED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 systematic feature-by-feature pass): a batch color-region check found this block's committed shape was roughly 55-85m too far south and somewhat too wide versus the diagram's actual fill. Re-measured programmatically instead of by eye: isolated this legend color (RGB [128,193,219]) across the combined H1/H2 area, split at the real internal divider (the dashed sub-division line at pixel x~1701-1746, using its midpoint x~1723 as the H1/H2 boundary), and extracted a clean rectangular contour (OpenCV) for this block at pixel (1466,1300)-(1723,1462). Converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. Re-confirmed zero overlap with Potrero Block 3/4 (the cross-site fix above still holds with this new, smaller shape) and zero overlap with H2. CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (street/curb re-anchoring pass, prompted by a user question about validation process consistency): this block's own north edge was directly confirmed, by rendering it against Esri World Imagery, to sit on top of real, currently-paved, actively-used street pavement (visible lane markings and/or vehicles in the satellite image), not a corner-lot sliver -- one of several Pier 70 blocks found this way after this project switched its real-street reference from OSM (community-traced, name-matched ways) to DataSF's own official Street Centerline / Curbs and Islands datasets (src/street_geometry.py), which for the first time gave an accurate enough curb position to see it. Clipped via shapely difference() against the corrected real-street buffer (6.8m centerline half-width, empirically measured against real curb data near Pier 70 -- see street_geometry.py); area 4025 -> 2536 sq m. The clip's result was a MultiPolygon (the street cut disconnected a 114 sq m sliver from the main body); kept only the larger piece, consistent with how this project has handled the same situation elsewhere (Mission Rock Square, Potrero Block 7). This is a targeted correction of this block's street-facing edge, not a re-verified re-trace of its other edges, which still carry this site's usual diagram-transform uncertainty. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the Assessor identifiers named in this log (Building 14's footprint as blklot 4052001; Building 12's Assessor parcel as blklot 4114010) come from DataSF (Building Footprints and Assessor parcels; repo copies in data/raw), not from the D4D cited for this file. Blklot 4052001 is a legacy lot: DataSF retired it on 2018-10-02 (Assessor parcels, acdm-wktn), its footprints carry mblr SF4052001, and the footprint layer does not name any of them 'Building 14'. Blklot 4114010 is an active lot at 1070 Maryland St that DataSF does not name 'Building 12'; that identity rests on the address given in tenant sources. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built (Port Item 11A, Aug 2026: the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'), and no source read ties it to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor parcels include new lots created for the 28-acre district in 2019, without street addresses, but which lot (if any) is this block's was not established. It currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district. Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. Street-facing edge re-clipped 2026-09-17 against official curb-referenced street data -- see digitization_method.'; notes: 'Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see accuracy_caveat. Status planned: Port Item 11A (Aug 2026) says construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward.'.
